---
title: Predictor Transformations Specification
---

## Introduction

This specification provides details of the predictor transformations that are
part of the [Requirements document](requirements.qmd#predictor-transformations).

Inputs for models used by the Algorithm Viewer may optionally be put through
various transformations before inputted into the model. Examples of
transformations include centering, multiplying to obtain interaction terms, and
applying restricted cubic splines. The transformations supported by the
Algorithm Viewer, as well as how these transformations are specified, should
conform to the specifications in the
[Model Parameters](https://github.com/Big-Life-Lab/model-parameters) repository.

This section specifies how all these transformations should be calculated. In
code, the implementation should represent all input variables as a single
matrix, allowing transformation of multiple input vectors
with a single pass. Any time a derived variable is created it should be added
to the matrix.

## Model Steps File

The steps involved for transforming the input data are specified in the [Model
Steps
File](https://big-life-lab.github.io/model-parameters/2-model-parameter-files.html#model-steps-file).
This file includes a list of steps along with a file path for the details
specific to that step. The steps are performed in sequence. Below is an example
Model Steps File:

| step        | fileType | filePath         |
|-------------|----------|------------------|
| dummy       | N/A      | dummy.csv        |
| rcs         | N/A      | rcs.csv          |
| interaction | N/A      | interactions.csv |
| center      | N/A      | center.csv       |
| logistic    | N/A      | logistic.csv     |

In the following sections, examples of the contents of the files specified in
the `filePath` column are shown.

## dummy Step

The [dummy
step](https://big-life-lab.github.io/model-parameters/2-model-parameter-files.html#dummy-step-file)
creates binary dummy variables from a categorical variable.

| origVariable | catValue | dummyVariable         |
|--------------|----------|-----------------------|
| smoker_type  | 0        | non_smoker            |
| smoker_type  | 1        | current_smoker        |
| smoker_type  | 2        | former_smoker         |

The above table can be expressed in code as:

```R
non_smoker <- as.integer(smoker_type == 0)
current_smoker <- as.integer(smoker_type == 1)
former_smoker <- as.integer(smoker_type == 2)
```

## center Step

The [center
step](https://big-life-lab.github.io/model-parameters/2-model-parameter-files.html#centering-step-file)
centers a variable by subtracting a center value.

| origVariable | centerValue | centeredVariable | centeredVariableType |
|--------------|-------------|------------------|----------------------|
| age          | 40          | age_C            | cont                 |
| diet_score   | 4           | diet_score_C     | cont                 |

The above table can be expressed in code as:

```R
age_C <- age - 40
diet_score_C <- diet_score - 4
```

## rcs Step

The [restricted cubic spline (rcs)
step](https://big-life-lab.github.io/model-parameters/2-model-parameter-files.html#restricted-cubic-spline-rcs-step-file)
applies a restricted cubic spline to a variable.

| variable | rcsVariables                              | knots              |
|----------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------|
| clc_age  | clc_age_rcs_1;clc_age_rcs_2;clc_age_rcs_3 | 24;40;57;74        |

The following code will apply the above RCS table to the input variable,
resulting in three new output variables (as specified in the `rcsVariables`
column):

```R
calculate_rcs <- function(x, knots) {
  k <- length(knots)
  res <- data.frame(rcs.1 = x)
  for (j in 1:(k - 2)) {
    kd <- (knots[k] - knots[1])^(2 / 3) # (knot_k-knot_1)^(2/3)

    vec1 <- x - knots[j] # X-knot_j

    val2 <- knots[k - 1] - knots[j] # knot_{k-1}-knot_j
    vec2 <- x - knots[k] # X-knot_k

    val3 <- knots[k] - knots[j] # knot_k-knot_j
    vec3 <- x - knots[k - 1] # X-knot_{k-1}
    val4 <- knots[k] - knots[k - 1] # knot_k-knot_{k-1}

    vec_j <- pmax(vec1 / kd, 0)^3 +
      (val2 * pmax(vec2 / kd, 0)^3 - val3 * pmax(vec3 / kd, 0)^3) / val4

    res$new <- vec_j
    names(res)[ncol(res)] <- paste0("rcs.", j + 1)
  }
  res <- as.matrix(res)
  return(res)
}

knots <- strsplit("24;40;57;74", ";")
knots <- as.numeric(unlist(knots))
rcs <- calculate_rcs(clc_age, knots)
clc_age_rcs_1 <- rcs[, 1]
clc_age_rcs_2 <- rcs[, 2]
clc_age_rcs_3 <- rcs[, 3]
```

## interaction Step

The [interaction
step](https://big-life-lab.github.io/model-parameters/2-model-parameter-files.html#interaction-step-file)
multiples two or more variables to get a new interaction variable.

| interactionVariable     | interactingVariables    | interactionVariableType |
|-------------------------|-------------------------|-------------------------|
| AgeXCancer              | Age;Cancer              | cont                    |
| AgeXCancerXHypertension | Age;Cancer;Hypertension | cont                    |

The above interaction table is represented in code as:

```R
AgeXCancer <- Age * Cancer
AgeXCancerXHypertension <- Age * Cancer * Hypertension
```

## logistic Step

The logistic step applies a logistic model to the existing variables. The
logistic equation has an intercept and coefficients for each variable. This
step is usually applied to the input variables after all transformations are
performed; it is equivalent to passing the variables into a logistic equation
to get a final output. In some cases, the user may instead want to pass the
transformed variables into an R model that performs the same operation. The
`Intercept` variable in the table below is a reserved word to represent the
intercept of the model.

| variable                   | coefficient |
|----------------------------|-------------|
| Intercept                  | 1           |
| clc_age_rcs_1_C            | 1.5         |
| clc_age_rcs_2_C            | -1          |
| clc_age_rcs_3_C            | 1           |
| diabx_1_C                  | 2           |
| clc_age_rcs_1_by_diabx_1_C | 0.1         |
| clc_age_rcs_2_by_diabx_1_C | -0.2        |
| clc_age_rcs_3_by_diabx_1_C | 3           |

The above logistic table is represented in code as:

```R
t <-
    1 +
    1.5 * clc_age_rcs_1_C +
    -1 * clc_age_rcs_2_C +
    1 * clc_age_rcs_3_C +
    2 * diabx_1_C +
    0.1 * clc_age_rcs_1_by_diabx_1_C +
    -0.2 * clc_age_rcs_2_by_diabx_1_C +
    3 * clc_age_rcs_3_by_diabx_1_C

logistic_output <- 1 / (1 + exp(-t))
```
